newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lonrho miners to protest S.Africa bombings.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho miners to protest S.Africa bombings.

text.p: Union members at Lonrho Plc platinum mines will stage a mass meeting on Thursday to protest against the alleged involvement of white miners in series of recent bombings, the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) said on Tuesday.

NUM said in a statement that Lonrho management confirmed on Tuesday that two white men held by police in connection with the bombings in South Africa's North West province last weekend, were employed by the company.

"We feel bound to take a position on this, since these acts of terror could ultimately affect our members. We expect the company to take a stand as well, since the commercial explosives used were likely to be stolen from the mine," NUM said.

The union said its members from Lonrho mines would hold a mass meeting on Thursday "to discuss and protest in a peaceful manner against the management's refusal to denounce the actions of this bombings".
Mine management was not immediately available for comment.
Police arrested two white mineworkers on Sunday after the three blasts in and around the platinum mining town of Rustenburg.
The two later appeared in court where they were refused bail and ordered to appear again on January 10.
